governing_text: An Extraction, the analysis of one paragraph under passages/FORMAT.md, is the source of every paragraph Move, and it is written by a fixed row on the shared supervisor with a run record rather than by a session, so that a wrong Move can be traced to the Extraction or to the ingest and the stage can be run again on the same input. [implemented-against: passages/FORMAT.md "The paragraph unit", copied 2026-10-15]
licensed_by: kogaki#1384 -- owner decision 2026-10-15: "I want the Prompts used by Composer and for file generation to be fixed in the Harness, not in SKILL instructions. Extraction seems particularly important, so we should establish a fixed Prompt for it." The row belongs to the Move-Extraction Playground and changes no production executable; whether a production Extractor adopts it is a separate decision.

judge.note: Every unit is a headless session, a `claude -p` child that runs with no tools (`--tools ""`), spawned by the shared Detached Job supervisor (src/workflow/detached-job.mjs). The model and both bounds NAME THE BRIEF'S SETTINGS, because the Issue gives this row the same bounds as the Brief's. `KOGAKI_JUDGE_CLI` replaces the resolved binary FOR FIXTURES ONLY.

job.note: ONE JOB PER PARAGRAPH, ONE UNIT PER JOB, run in the Leg's order, and after it the paragraph's content-bound job (kogaki#1614) and then its constraints job (kogaki#1698), on the same bounds (kogaki#1583): paragraph N's input carries the names paragraphs 1 to N-1 took, so N cannot start before N-1 is written; the state-bound job is retired with the reader table (kogaki#1699). A call past `brief.call_limit_s` is stopped and spends one round, a refused answer spends one, an unreadable answer is asked again without spending one, and a paragraph that has spent `brief.unit_rounds` stops the run naming the paragraph and its last refusal; the Extractions already written stay.

extraction_unit.note: The one call per paragraph (kogaki#1384). `src/move-extraction-playground/extract.mjs` renders this row through the shared `judgePrompt` renderer, FORMAT.md verbatim above the input marker, and the paragraph's own input below it; `validateExtractionUnit` reads the answer back against FORMAT and `extractionFileText` writes it as FORMAT's YAML record, `<name>.yaml` (kogaki#1413), so `tools/move_ingest.py passage --from-extraction` reads it unchanged through the same YAML module; `extractionMarkdown` renders the record for reading on the Move-Extraction Playground. The fields the Harness can count or knows -- `unit`, `length`, `status` -- and each Segment's quoted `opening` words are written by the Harness, never asked.
extraction_unit.governing: passages/FORMAT.md, "The paragraph unit" and "The Extraction"; kogaki#1384; kogaki#1698

content_bound_unit.note: The second call per paragraph, before the constraints call (kogaki#1614, the owner's reading of 2026-10-26). `src/move-extraction-playground/extract.mjs` issues it after the paragraph's Extraction record passes, and its input is the paragraph's sentences, each Segment's `content` clause beside its sentence, and `subject_nouns` as the allowed vocabulary, and nothing of the general fields: no `manner`, `breaks` or earlier paragraph. `validateContentBoundUnit` reads the answer back; a Segment judged unbound refuses the Extraction, and the refusal is put back into the Extractor's next round verbatim, within the Extractor's own round budget. The verdicts are written onto the record as `content_bound`, one entry per Segment. No schema file is rendered: nothing of FORMAT is this call's input.
content_bound_unit.governing: passages/FORMAT.md, "The paragraph unit", rule 7 (the `content` clause is the one field bound to the source); kogaki#1614

constraints_unit.note: The third call per paragraph, in the place the obligation call held (kogaki#1698, owner ruling 2026-11-06: the constraints a Move carries are one key with two sides, `takes` and `leaves`, over four closed kinds, read by judgment). `src/move-extraction-playground/extract.mjs` issues it after the paragraph's Extraction record passes the content-bound call, and its input is the four kinds with their definitions (`MOVE_CONSTRAINT_KINDS` in src/move-validate.mjs), each Segment's `content` clause (kogaki#1926), and the record's `takes` and `leaves`: no Passage, no sentence, no `subject_nouns`. `validateConstraintsUnit` reads the answer's shape back; an entry judged unsupported, or a thing a Segment leaves that no entry names, refuses the Extraction naming the entry or the Segment, and the refusal is put back into the Extractor's next round verbatim, within the Extractor's own round budget. No schema file is rendered: nothing of FORMAT is this call's input.
